key_insight: Laser oscillation trajectory shapes molten-pool energy distribution and flow, with suitable paths improving droplet-transfer stability in aluminum double-wire welding.
engineering_relevance: Coordinating laser power, oscillation settings, and wire feed could support more stable weld formation and precise process control.
method: Investigate coupled effects of laser power, oscillation parameters, and wire feeding speed.
Use high-speed imaging to observe molten-pool flow, droplet transfer, and metal filling.
Compare circular, ∞-shaped, and figure-eight trajectories to inform an energy–pool behavior–weld quality model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports real-time imaging observations and qualitative trajectory-dependent changes, but provides no numerical quality metrics or validation results.
watch_item: The coupled model is presented as an aim; no AI method or validated optimization framework is described in the abstract.
paper_title: Study on the transition behavior and forming process of oscillating laser double-wire welding of aluminum alloy
